validation.notes: Repaired packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts: recoverToolInvocation now replays a safe/safe effect_pending call instead of applying a blanket never-replay rule. The faulty guard was the dead-code short circuit `if (false && !cancelled && call.replay === "safe" && tool?.replay === "safe")`, which made every recovered tool effect fall through to the interrupted-checkpoint path; the minimal fix removes the leading `false &&` and leaves the conditional restrictions (`!cancelled`, persisted intent replay === "safe", live declaration replay === "safe") untouched. With the guard live, safe replay keeps the required ordering: clearReplayCheckpoint (deletes the stale pendingToolOutput value and re-reads the persisted args from operationToolArgs) runs before performToolInvocation, and publishToolOutcome settles the freshly produced result afterwards, so the durable checkpoint is cleared before invocation and the real outcome replaces it once the effect completes. `.prale-eval/regression.mjs` loads the real TypeScript module through the read-only `.prale-eval/subject.mjs` boundary fakes and asserts on observable event ordering rather than printed output: (1) safe intent + safe declaration, not cancelled -> events exactly [clear, invoke, effect-complete, publish] with a non-error "effect-result" outcome and no interruption marker; (1b) same ordering with an async effect; (2) cancelled safe/safe -> [read, publish], error outcome, no clear/invoke; (3) safe intent but "never" declaration -> interrupted checkpoint outcome, no replay; (4) recorded "never" intent with safe declaration -> interrupted, no replay; (5) missing tool declaration -> interrupted, no replay; (6) tool without an explicit replay policy -> interrupted, no replay. Interrupted cases additionally assert the durable checkpoint content ("durable-progress") and details ({step:2}) survive plus the trailing interruption marker. Verified bidirectionally: with the fix in place the script exits 0 (9 assertion groups pass); after temporarily restoring the original `false &&` fault the script fails immediately with AssertionError on `not cancelled (safe intent, safe declaration)` (actual events [read, publish] vs expected [clear, invoke, effect-complete, publish]), then the fix was restored and the run re-confirmed zero. The script resolves the workspace root from its own URL, so it does not depend on the invocation cwd. No dependencies were installed and no network was used; Node v24.14.0 provides TypeScript stripping and node:vm SourceTextModule. The repo's own vitest suites were not run because workspace dependencies are not installed, which is why the standalone assertion script is the focused validation.
